entityDescription: Seascape Belgium offers services to marine offshore and coastal operators, managers, policy makers and funders focusing on knowledge based solutions for sustainable management and development of our seas and oceans. Our expertise includes developing solutions for issues related to ocean governance, marine pollution, coordination of ocean observing and marine monitoring efforts, marine research infrastructures, management of marine data and information as well as facilitating Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) processes at the national, sea-basin and pan-European level. Seascape Belgium staff have long standing experience with science communication, event organisation, stakeholder engagement and facilitation of science-policy interfaces. We work alongside leading scientists around the world, and are partners in a number of major European research programmes addressing marine issues and opportunities. GIVE is a visionary design and engineering startup based in Athens, that started at the end of 2016. We provide technical innovation, product design, and advanced engineering analysis, specialized in the whole range of advanced engineering analysis, ranging from lightweight materials, structural analysis & optimization all the way to CFD, multi-body dynamics, electromagnetics and more. Through a solid experience in the world of the automotive, aerospace and motorsports, we derived speed and accuracy, as well as a passion for beautiful detail and efficient performance. We have been involved in a wid range of projects focused manily in the automotive and aerospace fields, while we have been also heavily involved in project work for the energy sector. Our work concerns advanced analysis, such as statics, non-linear structural analysis, FRA and modal analysis, crash (dynamic) behavior), composites, coupling of structural analysis with multi-body dynamics, etc, while optimization (topology, topography, free size, generic, etc) and CFD have also been critical to our business so far.

The company - founded in October 2016 - has been supported by own financial investments and earnings coming from our project work (contract work for the industry) that have all been “bootstrapped” back to our own R&D in the fields of vehicle electrification and product development. In 2019 Elin Verd became a minority shareholder with a first-round investment into GIVE (creation of holding company PBOT), helping develop a prototype electric vehicle (today at TRL7), as well as a solid business concept and strategy behind it. GIVE’s turnover has been increasing since 2016, with our estimation being that this pattern of growth will be maintained due to our products/services maturity status.

Besides however the contracted work, we believe it is imperative to stay close to relevant R&D projects, and GIVE has been involved in both national and international research calls. Currently we have been accepted in a national call for future development of energy management systems with integration of different energy sources (program ICBase), while we are also working on a EUROSTAR collaborative project with partners from Cyprus and Korea for the design, analysis and production (including prototyping and testing) of a hydrogen powered inspection drone (HyFly).Furthermore, we have created an internal program so as to stay close to the academia supporting two internships each year, PhD and master theses (currently we are the industrial supervisor of a PhD on autonomous driving) as well as a number of student teams that GIVE helps mainly with technical help and support (formula student, moto student, etc.). Keeping close to the academia brings us not only closer to the current state-of-the-art, but also close to the best students and ‘pool’ of talent. We are currently also awaiting response from a Marie Curie research program for the support of 4 industrial PhD researchers.

Open Thing CIC will provide benefit to individuals, families and businesses across the UK through improved air quality, stronger community links and promoting and encouraging environmental sustainability. Open Thing CIC will develop open-source devices and software for the benefit of this community. Individuals and groups will be able to access designs, instructions, kits and complete devices and a virtual community sharing information. Through Open Thing devices and software they can learn about the environment of their local area, and compare this to other sources of data across the UK and globally, and the other Open Thing devices. Through a simple dashboard, everyone will be able to understand how our daily cycle changes the world around us and measure how behaviour changes impact this. For example, kits to monitor air quality, which collects data to a dashboard showing how human behaviour (such as idling cars) impacts on air quality. The WHO has declared air pollution as the biggest environmental threat to global health, resulting in 7 million premature deaths a year. Seeing graphically how idling raises pollutants such as Nitrous Oxide in the air in real-time will empower schools and communities to inform and change behaviour. 

 enabling community/society to understand their impact on the environment 
 enrich information about how our behaviour impacts on the environment 
 change behaviour through informed feedback

The Institute is a centre of fundamental research in physical chemistry, electrochemistry and chemical physics (short history). The research work is characterized by many cross-links both within the Institute and also with other institutions in Europe, the U.S.A., Japan and other parts of the world. Much of the scientific work is concerned with fundamental research, but several groups, in particular in catalysis and electrochemistry, are also making contributions in more applied aspects. Besides the research activities the Institute is strongly involved in training of both undergraduate and graduate students, supervising their diploma and Ph.D. theses, and in teaching at universities.
In the Institute work at present about 165 full-time employees and approximately 45 graduate students. Roughly 70 per cent of the personnel are engaged in research, the remaining staff provides technical and administrative services.
Members of the Institute publish each year approximately 250 research papers, for the most part in impacted international journals (in 2017: 159 articles in journals with an average impact factor of 4.84), several books or chapters in monographs, and a number of communications in proceedings of scientific meetings.

The ambition is to offer clinical lab performance with the ease-of-use of a pregnancy test at a consumer price tag.
Antelope Dx offers a diagnostic testing device that performs accurate tests at home, in less than 15 minutes. It allows the individual to have on-the-spot access to key health parameters where and when it matters: testing accurately, yet in an affordable, lifestyle way. Today, only 2 successful home tests are available, the glucose test and the pregnancy test. They measure highly abundant proteins and are not complex. It is a difficult combination to bring highly accurate, easy to use tests at an affordable price tag for the individual at home. This is exactly what Antelope aims to do.

Photonic chips, complex measurements at low-cost
The recipe for success lies predominantly in the architecture of the Antelope consumable and reader. The Antelope platform is based on an innovative lab-on-chip technology that can perform a sensitive test on any bodily fluid, without requiring complex user operations or sample preparation.

This approach allows us to rapidly deploy low-cost, real-time,high-density air quality monitoring networks which complement governmental infrastructure.
